title: Round 20 (v3.2): fan back and torso both kept and combined, mean 5.447 to 5.495
lede: 2026-10-02. The first real gain since round 13. The round took 65 minutes and about 73M tokens, both kept orders combined cleanly by recipe merge in 6 minutes.
items: R04 fan back (audit gap 1): the round 17 clump branch, rebased onto the current model, replaced the crumpled shard bowl with overlapping pointed locks flowing out and down from a crown tuft, and the profile picket of cones with a band of leaf locks. R04 5.0 to 6.4. Its crown tuft spikes show in the front view and cost the fan front one step (R03 6.4 to 5.7), carried as a debt for the next fan front order.

R06 torso (audit gap 5), built with the new section loft: the belly band and belt crease are gone, the waist pinch is softer and the chest a little deeper. Kept on a better verdict, but no torso criterion moved: in profile it is still close to a plank.
The audit-led order picker chose the two top-ranked regions with ready tools, as intended. Both builders used the sweep, the seam check and the rebase.

title: Round 19 (one round after the v3.1 system changes): neck join kept, head reverted
lede: 2026-10-02. Weighted mean stays 5.447; the neck was kept on the critic verdict without a criterion moving. Round 19 cost about 90M tokens in 2 h 21 min, 51M of it the two toolsmiths.
items: R05 neck, worked at the head-body join for the first time: the head cut moved up and the fusion window raised, so the collar ring at the top of the neck melted away and the nape notch got shallower. Kept on a better verdict. It took 8 minutes and 3M tokens with no component rebuild, the cheapest order the loop has run.
R01 head shape: a skull ellipsoid raised the crown, but the dome barely clears the fan rims and the chin turned broad; judged the same and reverted after 81 minutes.
Toolsmiths built the fan front clump tool (R03) and the trunk section loft (R06) before the round, both smoke-tested and ready, but neither region was ordered this round.

Found and fixed tonight: recipe steps that pointed at files later rewritten (the R03 spec and the hind paw script), a containment zone too shallow for the fan front, and mangled paths in the toolsmith prompt.

title: Round 17: two orders, both reverted; the system learned two things
items: R04 ear fan rear, rebuilt as a clump volume (the new method): the critic judged it better, since the shard tiles and tooth rim became clumps flowing outward and down, but no R04 criterion moved and the rear needles cost the fan front one criterion, so the ratchet reverted it.
R09 hind paws: domed instep and claws from the toe tips, but the claws shrank to pin dots and an ankle collar appeared; the critic called it the same, so it was reverted.

Builder effort trial: the medium-effort twin of the R04 order used about 30 percent fewer tokens and was judged worse (it flattened the fan top into a shelf). One sample, so builders stay at high effort for now.
System change from this round: a reverted candidate the critic judged better becomes the starting point of the next order for that region, so a new method is not thrown away after one build.

System change from this round: the face scored 8.3 on the checklist while the audit ranked its slit profile eye third, so regions above the pass bar with a top-ten structural audit gap are now reopened, and the critic is shown the audit rows. Both changes start at round 19.

title: Loop v3 kickoff: what the fresh audit says is most wrong (assembled-0458)
lede: 2026-10-01. The v3 loop started from assembled-0458 with a fresh independent audit, ranked by how much each gap stops the model reading as the sheet. The rounds started without waiting; reply if the order looks wrong and I will change course. The tails are held, as you asked.
items: R04 (structural): Back and rear oblique: the fan's back is crumpled shards and thorns on a smooth shell, with a continuous pale rim along the lower edge and flat cut end planes, so it reads as a crumpled-paper bowl or nest with the head dome sunk behind seams. The outline already fits, so this is all construction.

R03 (structural): Front and three-quarter: the fan front is hard shards with serrated thorn edges and flat leaf facets. The inner tufts are white faceted blades with dark empty slots behind them, not one soft volume of pointed locks with a fluffy pale cup.

R02 (structural): Side and three-quarter: the eye shows as a narrow slanted slit pinched by a hard cheek and brow ridge, which looks angry or squinting. The sheet's profile eye is a tall oval about a third of head height (visible eye over head height about 0.15 vs 0.33, estimate).

R12: All views: a hard, jagged, high-frequency fan sits on a completely smooth bare vinyl body with no cheek, chest, forearm or calf coat masses, so the model mixes two levels and two idioms of construction against the sheet's one soft coat.

R06 (structural): Side view: the trunk is a straight vertical plank with no S curve or rib cage volume. Chest depth at .36 is 0.131 vs 0.168H, waist depth 0.106 vs 0.082H (1.30x), chest over waist 1.07 vs 1.54.

R03 (structural): Side view: the ear is a ragged column of shards with a row of tooth-like spikes down its back edge, and no pale inner cup is visible. The sheet shows a round shaggy disc with the cup opening forward and outward.

R07 (structural): Front and side: the forepaw is a small closed fist about as wide as the wrist, with fused digits and short spikes on its underside. The sheet's paw is about 0.6x wider than the model's (about 0.033 vs 0.055H, estimate) with separate digits and long claws from the tips. Posed arm IoU .867 fails.

R01 (structural): Front: the face is a broad block, with a flat forehead running straight between the ear roots, a square jaw and no skull dome rising between the ears (crown above the inner rim about 0.0 vs 0.02H, estimate).

R02: Front at full figure scale: the eyes read as near-round discs (height over width about 1.2 vs 1.5) with an even ring and a small centred pupil, so they stare like googly eyes. The sheet has tall ovals, a heavier upper lid and a large iris glancing to one side.

R05: Back and neck rear: a flat horizontal shoulder yoke with knobbed corners, a raised ledge across the shoulder blades and a collar ring at the top of the neck read athletic. The outline heights already match the sheet's sloped shoulders, so this is sculpt.

R09 (structural): Front: four near-equal toe beads in a straight row on a flat slab. Side: a low slipper with a vertical cliff heel and no domed instep, with the claws standing on the toe fronts instead of curving out of the tips. Posed foot IoU .647 fails.
R08: Side and front: a second swell on the back of the shin just above the heel and a knob at the knee. The widths now pass, but the posed shin IoU (.643) and thigh IoU (.830) fail.
R07: Side: the shoulder cap juts as a box and the outer upper arm carries a hard-edged flat lit strip, instead of a round arm blending into a rounded shoulder.

R02: Front and profile: a crust of small lumps rings the lower face, and a large flat cheek plate with hard edges sits behind the muzzle in profile, where the sheet has a smooth face with soft cheek tufts.
R06 (structural): Side and back: the rump barely projects behind the thigh line and the visible buttock has no fold. The tails partly hide this, so it needs a check with the tails hidden.
R08 (structural): Front rest pose: the feet are much wider apart than the sheet's (foot centre spacing at .98 is 0.44 vs 0.31H), giving a wider A stance. The posed fit mostly corrects it.
